gates.evidence: The surface is s19 (Settings) and the trigger is reaching for Upgrade to Luzia+.
The proposal uses a 15-second game unlock (SIM-RWD) for in-app time-boxed subscription features.
The offer uses gain framing ('unlock 30 minutes') with an explicit decline option ('No thanks').
The primary CTA is 'Play to try', providing explicit opt-in.
Body states: 'Play a 15-second game to unlock 30 minutes of Upgrade to Luzia+ today.'
Trigger is on Settings (s19), not interrupting any AI response.

scores.evidence: The proposal targets the Upgrade to Luzia+ upsell on Settings (m1, m23), offering a time-boxed sample, but the reward description mentions viewing favorite messages without an account, creating a mismatch.

The proposal attempts to bypass account creation / sign-up walls for account-only features like favorite messages through an ad, which violates the principle that an ad never stands in for creating an account.
While it time-boxes the sample to 30 minutes and caps it at twice a day, offering account-only features or subscription features via ads without an account undermines account creation.
Code-computed cost to serve is $0.0000 (none), well within net revenue per view ($0.0090-$0.0150 US mid eCPM haircut).
Settings (s19) and upgrade upsells are frequent touchpoints, but gating on settings taps has moderate reach.
Maps to SIM-RWD unit with button entry, SSV, and remote config.
References actual screen s19, Upgrade to Luzia+, and economy items r1, w1 from the digest.
Caps at 2 per day with a 60-minute cooldown.
Defines primary metric (sample opt-ins and subscription conversion), guardrails (-3% plan conversion, D7 retention), and a 10% user-level holdout for 4 weeks.

requiredChanges: Remove the attempt to use rewarded ads as a substitute for account creation or unlocking account-only features like favorite messages.
Ensure the reward strictly grants a time-boxed entitlement to Luzia+ subscription features rather than bypassing account walls.
parsed.topConcern: The proposal violates the core rule that an ad never stands in for creating an account or unlocking account-only features (viewing favorite messages), attempting to bypass account walls instead of sampling subscription features.
